## Paper

The Effect of Rewards and Sanctions in Provision of Public Goods

## World

public_goods

## Institution

Contribution matching and penalty/reward schedules.

## Agent type

Public-goods participants / learning agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Rewards and sanctions can change provision but may be costly or crowd out intrinsic incentives.

## Learning setup

Repeated contribution/extraction with externally modified rewards or penalties.

## Metrics

Welfare, contribution, sustainability, reward payments, penalty costs, state-change classification.

## Main result

Rewards and sanctions have different behavioral effects; sanctions are more effective in sustaining cooperation; rewards lead to a modest increase in group allocations but are less sustained over time

## What they prove

The paper provides experimental evidence that rewards and sanctions can have asymmetric behavioral effects in repeated public-goods provision. Treat this as evidence about the tested experimental setting, not a formal theorem for all incentive schemes.

## What they only simulate

Experimental behavior under reward and sanction treatments in repeated public-goods interactions.

## What they do NOT test

Long-term sustainability of reward systems; complex interactions between rewards and sanctions in diverse institutional settings

## What we need to reproduce

Separate welfare-improving cooperation from costly reward accounting under contribution matching and sanctions.

## How our project differs

The paper studies experimental reward/sanction provision. This repo uses parameterized institutions and validates state metrics.

## Implementation obligations

Contribution matching transfer accounting; penalty accounting; contribution/sustainability metrics; explicit state-changing versus reward-only classification.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Public Goods institution-effect validator; outputs/public_goods_full.

## Failure modes to audit

Counting transfers as welfare gains without state change; no cost accounting; no classification of institution effects.

## Project code comparison

Compare The Effect of Rewards and Sanctions in Provision of Public Goods to Public Goods contribution_matching and penalty_schedule rows. The repo should report whether state variables move, not just total reward.

## Extraction evidence

Text from the paper discussing the effects of rewards and sanctions on public goods provision; the use of rewards and sanctions in group allocations and earnings; the asymmetry in how rewards and sanctions affect payoffs
